key_insight: You can reconstruct 4D human motion and 3D scene layout using only wearable IMUs by repurposing large language models for non‑visual spatiotemporal reasoning, removing the need for cameras.
problem_solved: Addresses reliance on cameras for human and environment perception—mitigating privacy, safety, energy, and scalability concerns while enabling scene-aware understanding from ubiquitous wearable sensors.
method: Use sequences of wearable IMU measurements as the sole input modality (no cameras).
Repurpose large language models / sequence models to reason about spatiotemporal IMU data and infer scene-aware motion trajectories.
Decode model outputs into 4D reconstructions: temporally consistent human motion (pose over time) and a 3D scene layout around the person.
impact: Enables privacy-preserving, energy-efficient, and widely deployable sensing for AR, robotics, health monitoring, and safety-critical applications where cameras are impractical or undesirable.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: person with IMU sensors → sequence encoder (LLM) → 4D outputs (animated pose + 3D scene mesh).
Before/after comparison: camera-based perception vs IMU-only 4D reconstruction highlighting privacy and energy tradeoffs.
Timeline visualization: IMU signals mapped to a smooth temporal pose trajectory (showing continuity and scene interaction).
Icon set: privacy shield, low-power battery, wearable sensor, and 3D scene/pose glyphs to summarize benefits.
paper_title: Seeing Without Eyes: 4D Human-Scene Understanding from Wearable IMUs
paper_authors: Hao-Yu Hsu, Tianhang Cheng, Jing Wen, Alexander G. Schwing, Shenlong Wang
